audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating and carryRating were empty strings while breakdown.difficulty and report[14] both state 6/10 and 6/10.
audit.why: Blank rating fields render an empty badge against prose that already gives the numbers. Enum fields, exempt from the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart's side tokens contradicted its own why-lines on four rows. whys[2] says 'You take Level 3' above a 'Skill' token; whys[3] says 'swing back to Yasuo' above 'Skill'; whys[4] says 'leans Yasuo' above 'Dr. Mundo'; whys[6] says Yasuo's crit and Wind Wall outscale your regen, above 'Dr. Mundo'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Yasuo, Yasuo, Dr. Mundo, Yasuo, Yasuo, Dr. Mundo, Yasuo] and matches the whys[] text on every disputed row. This is the rarer shape where Dr. Mundo does NOT own the late game — Wind Wall and Sweeping Blade mean he survives forever and catches nothing — and the page had flattened it into the default 'my late game' template.
audit.corrected: Four flips proposed as one atomic group across both layers, plus the three phases[].why lines and breakdown.late that asserted the opposite.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall's effect on Infected Bonesaw appeared only in passing in the late-game prose, and never in the Key Ability Interactions block or the cooldown tracker.
audit.why: Dr. Mundo's Q is flagged projectile and Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds' on a 25/23/21/19/17 cooldown. That is the single decisive interaction of this lane: it deletes your only ranged tool, your only slow, and your entire poke pattern for four seconds at a time. It belongs in report[5] and the cooldown list, with the real numbers. Last Breath also requires an Airborne target — solo, that means his own Q3 tornado, which is the tell to watch.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, phases[4].why and phases[6].why now carry Wind Wall's 4s duration and 25s rank-1 cooldown, and Last Breath's Airborne requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Last Breath was listed as 80s in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].
audit.why: Riot data has it at 70/50/30. Maxed it is 30 seconds — less than half the figure the page gave. Planning a commit around an 80-second window when he has it back in 30 is how the player dies.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] told the player to use "E Blunt Force Trauma's true range".
audit.why: Dr. Mundo's E has range 0 in the kit data — it is not a ranged tool with a hidden reach, it is an auto-attack reset that empowers the next hit. 'True range' invites the player to step up expecting extra distance that does not exist. The packet's suspectName flag on the ability name itself is a false positive; Blunt Force Trauma is correct.
audit.corrected: Reworded to name the auto reset.
